chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud al-Ta'i, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the combatant (al-muharib), so I said to him, 'Our companions say that the Imam has a choice in it: if he desires, he cuts; if he desires, he crucifies; and if he desires, he kills.' He said, 'No! These are matters limited in the Book of Allah, Exalted and Majestic. So if he kills and seizes (property), he is killed and crucified; and if he kills and does not seize, he is killed; and if he seizes and does not kill, he is cut; and if he flees and is not able to be caught, then he is seized, he is cut, except if he repents. So if he repents, he is not cut.'

key_terms.الْإِمَام: The Imam (specifically the Imam of Justice who applies the law)
key_terms.الْمُحَارِب: Combatant (one who engages in qat' al-tariq/highway robbery)
key_terms.قَطَعَ: He cuts (referring to amputation of the hand)
key_terms.مَحْدُودَةٌ: Limited/Determined (fixed by divine law, not discretionary)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific hudud penalties for a combatant who kills and steals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi refutes the juristic view of arbitrary Imamate discretion by anchoring the penalties for al-muharib in the explicit textual hierarchy of Surah Al-Ma'idah. It establishes a precise legal matrix where the severity of punishment—execution, crucifixion, or amputation—is strictly determined by the combination of killing and property seizure, while highlighting repentance as a specific mitigator for the limb-cutting penalty.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Al Tai’y, from a man from our companions,

(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the combatant, so I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Our companions are saying that the Imam<sup>asws</sup> has a choice in it, if he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to he<sup>asws</sup> cuts, and if he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to he<sup>asws</sup> crucifies, and if he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to, he<sup>asws</sup> kills’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No! These things are Limited in the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. So if it is such that he has killed and seized (property, he would be killed and crucified; and when he has killed and die not seize (property), he would be killed; and when he seizes (property) and doe not kill, so he would be cut; and when he flees and is not able to be caught, then he is seized, he would be cut, except if he were to repent. So if he were to repent, he would not be cut’.
